To match the per capita level of exports of Singapore in the late 1980s, Egypt would have had to expand its exports to capture 23 percent of world trade—or significantly more than the merchandise exports of Japan and the United States combined.

Even the far more modest goal of matching South Korea, whose exports were worth $1,120 per capita in 1987, would have required Egypt to capture 2.35 percent of world trade. This would involve a forty-fold increase in nonoil exports, from an annual level at that time of about $1.25 billion to more than $52 billion.
zh: 这种认为东亚的解决办法为其他第三世界国家提供了模型的看法很奇特。
1987年，埃及的商品出口不到世界贸易的0.2%。其中三分之二以上是石油，而预计石油供应在未来几十年将下降。要达到新加坡1980年代后期的人均出口水平，埃及必须扩大到占世界贸易的23%——大大超过日本和美国的商品出口总和。
即使要达到一个远为温和的目标——赶上韩国1987年人均1,120美元的出口额——埃及也必须占据世界贸易的2.35%。这将要求非石油出口增加四十倍，从当时每年约12.5亿美元增至520亿美元以上。

en: There was no evidence that Europe’s demand for airlifted shipments of Egyptian cut flowers and winter tomatoes might grow by even a fraction of this amount. In the absence of the kind of far-reaching land reform carried out in South Korea, there was also no evidence that such export policies would be of any benefit to the landless and near-landless majority of rural Egyptians.

In fact other cases of agro-export policies suggest the opposite. For example, Brazil, which was “a stunning success as measured by investment in agrofood production and exports,” was also “a nightmare of evictions from the land, displacement of local food systems, hunger, and social unrest.”

Finally, as Streeten and others noted, this export-oriented solution was supposed to occur not during a period of enormous regional and global demand, such as that generated by Japanese growth and the Vietnam war during the period when the East Asian economies began to expand, but in a period of economic retrenchment during the 1980s, a period when a dozen or more large Third World countries were adopting similar remedies and competing for the same limited market.

In fact, Adelman’s economic modeling suggested that in the situation of depressed world trade an alternative policy of transferring wealth to medium and small farmers (via land reform, infrastructural investment, and higher producer prices) to stimulate rural employment and consumption would result in higher rates of growth and larger exports than export-led policies.
It would also produce a substantial redistribution of income from rich to poor.
zh: 没有证据表明欧洲对空运埃及切花和冬季番茄的需求会增长到这个数量的哪怕一小部分。在缺乏韩国那种深远土地改革的情况下，也没有证据表明这类出口政策会对埃及农村占多数的无地或少地者有任何好处。
事实上，农业出口政策的其他例子表明的恰恰相反。例如巴西，“以农业食品生产和出口投资衡量是惊人的成功”，同时也是“驱逐土地、取代地方粮食体系、饥饿与社会动荡的噩梦”。
最后，正如斯特里滕等人所指出的，这种出口导向的解决办法本应出现在区域和全球需求巨大的时期——例如东亚经济体开始扩张时期由日本增长和越南战争所产生的需求——而不是1980年代经济紧缩时期；那时已有十多个第三世界大国采取类似补救办法，争夺同一个有限市场。
事实上，阿德尔曼的经济模型表明，在世界贸易萧条的情况下，另一种政策——通过土地改革、基础设施投资和提高生产者价格把财富转移给中小农，以刺激农村就业和消费——会带来比出口导向政策更高的增长率和更大的出口。
它还会带来收入从富人向穷人的大幅再分配。

en: There is a second consequence of the way the imagery of the Nile valley and its people—and the larger discourse of development—constitute Egypt as a self-contained object. By setting out this sort of visual image of Egypt, the country is imagined as an object that exists apart from the discourse that describes it. The geographical metaphor that introduces the reports of an organization like USAID in Cairo evokes an entity “out there,” Egypt, laid out like a map as the object of the organization’s planning and knowledge. The organization itself, the metaphor suggests, is not an aspect of this object. It stands above the map of Egypt to measure and make plans, a rational center of expertise and policy making that forms no part of the object observed. USAID is not marked, so to speak, on the map.
zh: 尼罗河谷及其人民的意象——以及更广泛的发展论述——把埃及构成为自足对象，这还有第二个后果。通过展示这种埃及的视觉形象，这个国家被想象为一个独立于描述它的论述而存在的对象。美国国际开发署开罗机构之类组织的报告开篇所用的地理隐喻，唤起一个“存在于外部”的实体——埃及，像地图一样铺开，作为该组织规划和知识的对象。这个隐喻暗示，组织本身不是这一对象的一个方面。它站在埃及地图之上进行衡量和制定计划，是一个由专业知识和政策制定构成的理性中心，不属于所观察对象的一部分。可以说，美国国际开发署没有被标记在地图上。

en: Development discourse thus practices a self-deception—what Partha Chatterjee calls “a necessary self-deception,” for without it development could not constitute itself.

Development is a discourse of rational planning. To plan effectively, it must grasp the object of its planning in its entirety. It must represent on the plans it draws up every significant aspect of the reality with which it is dealing. A miscalculation or omission may cause the missing factor to disrupt the execution of the plan. Its calculations must even include the political forces that will affect the process of execution itself.
zh: 因此，发展论述实践着一种自我欺骗——帕沙·查特吉称之为“一种必要的自我欺骗”，因为若没有它，发展就无法构成自身。
发展是一种理性计划的话语。要有效计划，就必须完整把握其计划对象。它必须在所绘制的计划中再现它所处理的现实的每一个重要方面。一个误算或遗漏可能使缺失的因素扰乱计划的执行。它的计算甚至必须包括将影响执行过程本身的政治力量。

en: This calculation has a limit, however, which is where the self-deception is required. As Chatterjee points out, the political forces that rational planning must calculate affect not only the execution of plans but the planning agency itself. An organization like USAID, which must imagine itself as a rational consciousness standing outside the country, is in fact a central element in configurations of power within the country. Yet as a discourse of external rationality, symbolized as the consciousness that unfolds Egypt as a map, the literature of development can never describe its own place in this configuration of power.
zh: 然而，这种计算有一个限度，自我欺骗正是在此必要。正如查特吉所指出的，理性计划必须计算的政治力量不仅影响计划的执行，也影响计划机构本身。像美国国际开发署这样的组织必须把自己想象为一种站在该国之外、展开埃及地图的理性意识；它实际上是该国境内权力配置中的一个核心要素。然而，作为关于外部理性的话语——被象征为展开埃及地图的那种意识——发展文献永远无法描述自身在这种权力配置中的位置。

en: Consider the case of USAID’s decentralization program, designed to reduce the role of the state and encourage “democracy and pluralism”by channeling development funds to private initiatives at the village and district level. The report quoted earlier suggested that among the principal beneficiaries of these funds were local government officials, state agricultural engineers, and other members of the state bureaucracy. The other main beneficiaries, wealthy farmers, often entered into partnership with such officials.

Far from encouraging a “private sector” in opposition to the state, such programs made the state an even more powerful source of funds and site of patronage. The new accumulations of wealth were never more than semiprivate, for they were parasitic on this strengthened state structure.
zh: 以美国国际开发署的去中心化项目为例，该项目旨在减少国家的作用，并通过把发展资金输送给村庄和县一级的私人举措来鼓励“民主与多元主义”。前面引用的报告表明，这些资金的主要受益者包括地方政府官员、国家农业工程师和国家官僚机构的其他成员。另一个主要受益群体——富裕农民——常常与这类官员合伙。
这类项目远未鼓励出一个与国家对抗的“私营部门”，反而使国家成为更强大的资金来源和庇护场所。新的财富积累从来只是半私有的，因为它们寄生于这个被加强的国家结构。

en: A similar process was described by Robert Springborg at the national level. He gave the example of one recipient of USAID funds, a man who was chair of the Foreign Relations Committee of the State Advisory Council (Majlis al-Shura). He was from a family long involved in Egyptian politics and business and had a personal wealth of several million pounds. USAID provided him with two sizable loans to purchase American irrigation equipment for large tracts of reclaimed land he owned, parts of which he sold off immediately after the equipment was installed. Springborg concludes that “a large proportion of USAID private sector assistance has been utilized by those well connected within the state apparatus to turn quick profits”—to the extent that even USAID economists in Cairo became disillusioned with the program of private sector loans.

In chapter 9 we will meet several other private entrepreneurs who grew rich from USAID programs, including one multimillionaire in his thirties who gave a new meaning to the American program of “cost recovery” in health care.
zh: 罗伯特·斯普林博格在国家层面描述了类似的过程。他举了一个美国国际开发署资金接受者的例子：此人是国家协商会议（Majlis al-Shura）外交委员会主席。他出身于长期参与埃及政治和商业的家族，个人财富达数百万镑。美国国际开发署向他提供了两笔数额可观的贷款，用于为他拥有的大片改良土地购买美国灌溉设备，其中部分土地在设备安装后立即被他卖掉。斯普林博格的结论是，“美国国际开发署私营部门援助的很大一部分被国家机器内关系良好者用来赚取快钱”——以至于连开罗的美国国际开发署经济学家也对私营部门贷款计划不再抱幻想。
在第9章，我们将遇到另外几位因美国国际开发署项目而致富的私营企业家，包括一位三十多岁的千万富翁，他赋予了美国医疗“成本回收”计划一个新的含义。

en: These examples illustrate the characteristic limits of development discourse. The major goal of USAID programs in Egypt was to develop what is termed the “private sector.” The actual effect of these programs, however, was to strengthen the power of the state. This was not simply some fault in the design or execution of the programs. USAID itself is a state agency, a part of the “public sector,” and therefore worked in liaison with the public sector in Egypt. By its very presence within the Egyptian public sector it strengthened the wealth and patronage resources of the state. USAID was thus part of the problem it wished to eradicate. Yet because the discourse of development must present itself as a rational, disinterested intelligence existing outside its object, USAID could not diagnose itself as an integral aspect of the problem.
zh: 这些例子说明了发展论述特有的局限。美国国际开发署在埃及项目的主要目标，是发展所谓的“私营部门”。然而，这些项目的实际效果是加强了国家的权力。这不只是项目设计或执行中的某种缺陷。美国国际开发署本身就是一个国家机关，“公共部门”的一部分，因此与埃及的公共部门协同工作。正是由于它身处埃及公共部门之中，它加强了国家的财富和庇护资源。美国国际开发署因此成了它希望根除的问题的一部分。然而，由于发展论述必须把自己呈现为存在于其对象之外的理性、无私的智力，美国国际开发署无法把自身诊断这一问题的一个内在方面。

en: opposed to subsidies?
zh: 反对补贴？

en: This difficulty in seeing itself as a part of the scene reflected a much larger deception. The prevailing wisdom of organizations like the World Bank, the IMF, and USAID was that the problems of a country such as Egypt stemmed from the restrictions placed on the initiative and freedom of the private sector.

The program of “structural adjustment” these organizations attempted to impose on Egypt from the late 1970s, particularly following the 1985–86 collapse of oil prices, which left the country incapable of keeping up payments on its international debts, aimed to dismantle the system of state subsidies and controls and enable the private sector to flourish in the unrestricted freedom of “the market.” Prices Egyptians paid to consume, or received for producing, food, fuel, and other goods were to reflect prices in the international market.
zh: 这种难以把自身视为场景一部分的困难，反映了一个大得多的骗局。世界银行、国际货币基金组织和美国国际开发署之类组织的主流看法是，埃及这样的国家的问题源于对私营部门主动性和自由的限制。
这些组织从1970年代末开始试图强加于埃及的“结构调整”计划，特别是1985—86年油价暴跌使该国无法偿还国际债务之后强加的，旨在拆解国家补贴和控制体系，使私营部门能在“市场”不受限制的自由中蓬勃发展。埃及人为消费食品、燃料和其他商品所支付的价格，或为生产所获得的价格，要反映国际市场的价格。

en: Yet it hardly needs pointing out that world prices for most major commodities are determined not by the free interplay of “private” market forces but by the monopolies or oligopolies organized by states and multinational corporations. Oil prices are determined not by the users of cars and electricity but by the ability of producer states to coordinate quotas and price levels. The price of raw sugar (a major Egyptian industrial crop), whose volatility was described as more than twice that of any other commodity monitored by the World Bank, is determined largely by U.S. and other government price support programs. Only about 14 percent of world production is freely traded on the market.
The international market for aluminum, one of the main heavy industries in Egypt, also operates under extensive state controls.
zh: 然而几乎无需指出，大多数主要商品的世界价格不是由“私营”市场力量的自由互动决定的，而是由国家及跨国公司组织的垄断或寡头垄断决定的。石油价格不是由汽车和电力使用者决定的，而是由产油国协调配额和价格水平的能力决定的。原糖（埃及的一种主要经济作物）的价格波动被描述为世界银行监测的任何其他商品的两倍以上，而它主要由美国和其他政府的价格支持计划决定。世界市场上自由交易的只占世界产量的约14%。
铝是埃及主要重工业之一，其国际市场也在广泛的国家控制下运作。

en: Perhaps the most significant example is the world grain market. One of the arguments against Egypt producing the staple foods it needed was that it could not compete in the world market against the low grain prices of American farmers. Yet these prices were the product of subsidies and market controls. American agriculture, operating under an imperative of constant growth, had come to be dominated by giant corporations that supplied the inputs to farming and processed and marketed its products. By the 1980s more than three-quarters of the American farm supply industry was controlled by just four firms. Six corporations, all but one of them privately owned, controlled 95 percent of U.S. wheat and corn exports and 85 percent of total world grain trade.
As Congressional investigations had shown, the monopolies these firms enjoyed enabled them to control the market and administer prices.

Squeezed by these monopolies on both ends, inputs and marketing, American farmers found themselves having to grow ever larger quantities of crops merely to survive, investing constantly in new technologies and getting increasingly into debt. Since the 1930s, this accelerating treadmill had put more than two-thirds of the country’s farms out of existence—and continued to ruin them in the present.
zh: 也许最重要的例子是世界谷物市场。反对埃及生产其所需主粮的一个论点是，它无法在世界市场上与美国农民的低谷物价格竞争。然而这些价格是补贴和市场管制的产物。美国农业在持续增长的强制要求下运作，已为提供农业投入品、加工和销售其产品的巨型公司所支配。到1980年代，超过四分之三的美国农业供应产业仅由四家公司控制。六家公司——除一家外全部为私有——控制着美国小麦和玉米出口的95%以及世界谷物贸易总量的85%。
正如国会调查所表明的，这些公司享有的垄断使它们能够控制市场并操纵价格。
美国农民在投入品和销售两端都受这些垄断的挤压，发现自己不得不种植越来越大量的作物仅仅为了生存，不断投资于新技术，负债越来越重。自1930年代以来，这种加速的跑步机已使全国三分之二以上的农场不复存在——并且在当下继续毁掉它们。

en: To mitigate the system’s effects, the state introduced large subsidies, starting with the price supports and crop controls of the New Deal programs, followed by the subsidized exports of the postwar Marshall Plan, the Public Law 480 program (which financed up to 58 percent of U.S. grain exports during the 1950s and 1960s), and President Nixon’s 1972 New Economic Policy (which further subsidized exports, and boosted prices by paying farmers to take 62 million acres out of production, an area equal to ten times the total cultivated area of Egypt). As a result of these policies, by 1982 American grain was being sold at prices 40 percent below estimated average production costs, and keeping farmers afloat was costing $12 billion a year in state subsidies.

Despite the low producer prices, moreover, consumer prices remained so high that 40 million Americans required government subsidies to purchase food, costing a further $27 billion a year in federal funds.
Government export subsidies paid for middle- and upperclass consumers in non-Western countries to shift to a meat-centered diet and thus expand the market for American feed grains.

By the 1990s this system was collapsing. The United States and the European Union could no longer afford the ever increasing levels of state subsidy, new Third World agricultural exporters were cutting into the dominant countries’ market share, and transnational agro-industries were finding some of the restrictions on free trade an impediment to further growth and globalization. Short-term solutions were sought in a reorientation of trade into regional market blocs and a shift from price supports to income supports (which do not encourage excessive surplus). But following the U.S. Freedom to Farm Act of 1996, federal payments to farmers continued to rise, reaching an annual $23 billion—twice the level of 1982—by 1999.

There was no evidence of a long-term solution or an end to state subsidies and controls. As we have seen, the largest site in the world to be incorporated into this system of state-subsidized American farming was Egypt. The arm of the state that has organized this incorporation was USAID.
zh: 为减轻这一体系的影响，国家引入了大量补贴，首先是新政计划中的价格支持和作物控制，随后是战后马歇尔计划下的出口补贴、公共法480计划（1950年代和1960年代为美国谷物出口提供高达58%的资金），以及尼克松总统1972年的新经济政策（进一步补贴出口，并通过付钱让农民将6,200万英亩土地退出生产来抬高价格，这一面积相当于埃及全部耕地面积的十倍）。由于这些政策，到1982年，美国谷物以比估计平均生产成本低40%的价格出售，而维持农民生存每年要花费120亿美元的国家补贴。
此外，尽管生产者价格很低，消费者价格仍然高得使4,000万美国人需要政府补贴来购买粮食，每年又花费270亿美元联邦资金。
政府出口补贴为西方以外国家的中上层消费者转向以肉类为中心的饮食买单，从而扩大了美国饲料谷物的市场。

到1990年代，这一体系正在崩溃。美国和欧盟再也负担不起不断升级的国家补贴，新的第三世界农业出口国正在蚕食主导国家的市场份额，跨国农业产业发现自由贸易的某些限制妨碍了进一步增长和全球化。短期解决办法是把贸易重新导向区域市场集团，以及从价格支持转向收入支持（后者不鼓励过度过剩）。但在1996年美国《农业自由法》之后，联邦对农民的支付继续上升，到1999年达到每年230亿美元——是1982年水平的两倍。
没有证据表明存在长期解决办法，也没有证据表明国家补贴和控制会终结。如我们所见，世界上被纳入这一国家补贴的美国农业体系的最大地点就是埃及。组织这一纳入的国家之臂是美国国际开发署。

en: The self-deception of USAID discourse was not just that it set up an object called Egypt in which it could not recognize its own internal role. It is that this supposed object was caught up in a much larger configuration of power, a network of monopolies and subsidies misleadingly named the world “market,” of which USAID itself was but a subsidiary arm. An agency devoting itself to the cause of dismantling subsidies and promoting the “private” sector was itself an element in the most powerful system of state subsidy in the world.
zh: 美国国际开发署话语的自我欺骗，不仅在于它设定了一个名为埃及的对象，却无法在其中认出自己内在的角色。还在于这个所谓的对象被卷入了一个更大得多的权力配置，一个被误导性地称为世界“市场”的垄断与补贴网络，而美国国际开发署本身只是其中的一个附属分支。一个致力于拆解补贴和促进“私营”部门的机构，本身就是世界上最强大的国家补贴体系中的一个要素。

en: USAID’s role as a source of subsidies to American agriculture and industry can be seen by examining how it spent the $15 billion budget for “economic assistance” to Egypt from the start of its operations there in 1974–75 up to 1989 (see fig. 3). Almost every penny of this amount, it can be shown, was actually allocated to American corporations. Just over half the total, first of all, represents money spent by Egypt to purchase goods from the United States. The Public Law 480 Food Aid program and the Commodity Import Program, totaling about $7.7 billion up to 1989, enabled Egypt to purchase grain, other agricultural commodities, agricultural and industrial equipment, and other U.S. imports.

Egypt paid for about half the commodities in dollars, with the United States providing low-interest long-term credit. The other half were paid for immediately or on short-term credit, but in Egyptian pounds.
zh: 要看到美国国际开发署作为美国农业和工业补贴来源的角色，可以考察它从1974—75年开始在埃及运作到1989年期间，如何花掉150亿美元的“经济援助”预算（见图3）。可以证明，这笔钱几乎每一分实际上都分配给了美国公司。首先，总额的略超过一半是埃及用于从美国购买商品的资金。公共法480粮食援助计划和商品进口计划到1989年总计约77亿美元，使埃及能够购买谷物、其他农产品、农业和工业设备以及其他美国进口品。
埃及以美元支付约一半商品的费用，美国提供低息长期信贷。另一半以即时或短期信贷支付，但以埃及镑支付。

en: A further $1 billion of the total aid was also paid directly to the United States, this part by the U.S. government itself, in the form of so-called Cash Transfers used to keep up payments on Egypt’s military debt. United States law stipulated that all aid except food must be stopped to a country that falls more than a year behind in military debt repayments, as Egypt began to do in the winter of 1983–84.

The U.S. government responded to this threatened collapse of the system of subsidies to its own private sector by converting all subsequent military loans to grants, allocating the bulk of those grants for progress payments to itself on earlier Egyptian arms purchases, and instructing USAID in the meantime to circumvent the law by setting aside about $100 million a year from economic development funds as Cash Transfers, to be deposited in the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and then returned to Washington as Egypt’s monthly interest payments on its military debt.

When this illegal diversion of economic development funds for military purposes was discovered by Congress (thanks to the leak of a USAID cable to the Washington Post), the aid agency denied it was happening—but continued the practice. The law, an agency lawyer later admitted, “was an academic question, since actual CT [Cash Transfer] expenditures were untraceable.”
zh: 援助总额中另有10亿美元也是直接支付给美国的，这部分由美国政府自己支付，形式是所谓的“现金转移”，用于维持埃及军事债务的偿还。美国法律规定，对拖欠军事债务偿还超过一年的国家，必须停止除粮食以外的所有援助；埃及在1983—84年冬天开始出现这种情况。
面对对其本国私营部门补贴体系崩溃的威胁，美国政府的回应是把所有后续军事贷款转为赠款，将其中大部分赠款分配用于为本国早先埃及军火采购的进度付款，同时指示美国国际开发署绕过法律，每年从经济发展资金中拨出约1亿美元作为现金转移，存入纽约联邦储备银行，然后作为埃及每月军事债务利息支付返回华盛顿。
当这种非法挪用经济发展资金用于军事目的的行为被国会发现时（由于一份美国国际开发署电报泄露给《华盛顿邮报》），援助机构否认此事发生——但继续这样做。该机构的一名律师后来承认，这项法律“是一个学术问题，因为实际的现金转移支出无法追踪”。

en: Figure 3. U.S. economic assistance to Egypt, 1975–89. Source: USAID, Status Report (Cairo, 1989).
zh: 图3. 美国对埃及的经济援助，1975—89年。资料来源：USAID, Status Report (Cairo, 1989).
〔图内文字译释：图内：总额14,982,000,000美元；商品进口29%、公法480援助22%、现金转移7%、项目42%。〕

en: In 1987, when new accounting rules finally revealed the illegal diversion of funds, the U.S. government reversed itself and argued that such military use of economic aid was legal, on the grounds that 1) military debts, once incurred, became an “economic” and not a “military” question, and 2) in the case of Israel, Congress routinely repaid the U.S. Treasury Israel’s annual military debt out of economic assistance funds. Congress rejected the first argument, pointing out that by paying Egypt’s past military debts USAID was directly ensuring the supply of current military aid, and rejected the assumption underlying the second argument, that other countries could receive the same exemption from U.S. law enjoyed by Israel, as a gross misunderstanding of “the realities of this Congress and what happens up here with respect to Israel.”

USAID agreed, once again, to stop paying Egyptian military debts from its funds—but the following year was already asking to have the new accounting rules relaxed. In 1990, following the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait and further Egyptian debt defaults, the U.S. government wiped out Egypt’s entire $7.1 billion military debt, using Egypt’s political support for a war against Iraq to overcome Congressional opposition.
zh: 1987年，当新的会计规则最终揭示出资金的非法挪用，美国政府改变立场，声称这种将经济援助用于军事的做法是合法的，理由是：1）军事债务一旦产生，就成为一个“经济”而非“军事”问题；2）就以色列而言，国会例行从经济援助资金中替以色列偿还每年欠美国财政部的军事债务。国会拒绝了第一个论点，指出美国国际开发署通过偿还埃及过去的军事债务，直接确保了当前军事援助的供应；并拒绝第二个论点背后的假设——其他国家可以享有以色列那种美国法律豁免——认为这是对“本届国会的现实以及这里在以色列问题上发生的情况”的严重误解。
美国国际开发署再次同意停止用其资金偿还埃及军事债务——但第二年就已经请求放宽新的会计规则。1990年，在伊拉克入侵科威特和埃及进一步拖欠债务之后，美国政府勾销了埃及全部71亿美元军事债务，利用埃及对反伊拉克战争的政治支持来克服国会的反对。

en: Thus a total of $8.7 billion, or 58 percent of all U.S. economic assistance, was spent directly in the United States rather than on development projects in Egypt, and most of this “American aid” in fact represents money paid by Egypt to America.
zh: 因此总共87亿美元，即美国全部经济援助的58%，直接花在了美国，而不是埃及的发展项目上；其中大部分“美国援助”事实上是埃及支付给美国的钱。

en: The remaining 42 percent of U.S. economic assistance funds to Egypt, totaling $6.3 billion, were earmarked for development projects within the country (see fig. 4). Yet none of this money was transferred directly to Egypt. The entire amount, as far as one can tell, was spent in the United States, or on American contractors in Egypt. The major recipients of the funds were large American manufacturing, construction, and consulting firms. More than $1 billion went to corporations like General Electric, Westinghouse, and Overseas Bechtel to purchase thermal power turbines and electricity distribution systems. More than $1.5 billion went to U.S. engineering and construction firms to build sewage networks and drinking water plants. Three hundred million dollars went to American Telephone and Telegraph and other U.S. communications companies to supply telephone equipment for Cairo and Alexandria. More than $200 million went to Ferguson International of Cleveland, Ohio, and other U.S. firms for the construction of two cement plants. American agribusiness and engineering firms received multimillion dollar contracts to supply grain silos and fats storage facilities for the country’s expanded U.S. food imports. Dredging and earth-moving equipment was purchased from firms like Caterpillar, John Deere, and International Harvester. Westinghouse Health Systems received tens of millions of dollars to improve rural and urban “health delivery.” And hundreds of millions of dollars went to American universities and research institutes to provide training in agricultural sciences, management, and technology transfer.
zh: 美国对埃及经济援助资金剩余的42%，总计63亿美元，被指定用于该国境内的发展项目（见图4）。然而这些钱没有一分直接转给埃及。就所能判断的而言，全部款项都花在美国，或花在埃及的美国承包商身上。资金的主要接受者是美国大型制造、建筑和咨询公司。超过10亿美元流向通用电气、西屋电气和海外柏克德之类的公司，用于购买火力发电涡轮机和配电系统。超过15亿美元流向美国工程和建筑公司，用于建设污水管网和饮用水厂。3亿美元流向美国电话电报公司和其他美国通信公司，为开罗和亚历山大供应电话设备。超过2亿美元流向俄亥俄州克利夫兰的弗格森国际公司和其他美国公司，用于建设两座水泥厂。美国农业综合企业和工程公司获得数百万美元的合同，为该国扩大的美国粮食进口供应粮仓和油脂储存设施。疏浚和土方设备购自卡特彼勒、约翰迪尔和国际收割机之类的公司。西屋健康系统公司获得数千万美元，用于改善农村和城市的“卫生服务提供”。还有数亿美元流向美国大学和研究机构，用于提供农业科学、管理和技术转移方面的培训。

en: Many of these projects also required local payments within Egypt in Egyptian pounds. In 1988 such local implementation costs were said to amount to about E£200 million annually, equivalent then to just over $100 million, or about 10 percent of annual U.S. dollar aid for development projects.

But such payments were not made from U.S. dollar funds. Instead, local currency funds paid by the Egyptian government to purchase American imports under the Commodity Import Program, mentioned above, were used by USAID in Cairo to pay for all local costs. In other words, the local implementation expenses of development projects (and even the local operating costs of the USAID mission in Cairo) were paid by the Egyptian government, in exchange for commodities imported from the United States.
zh: 这些项目中有许多还需要在埃及境内以埃及镑支付当地费用。1988年，这种当地实施费用据说每年约为2亿埃镑，当时相当于略超过1亿美元，即用于发展项目的年度美元援助的约10%。
但这些付款并非来自美元资金。相反，开罗的美国国际开发署使用埃及政府根据上述商品进口计划购买美国进口品所支付的本地货币资金，来支付所有当地费用。换言之，发展项目的当地实施费用（甚至美国国际开发署开罗使团的当地运营费用）由埃及政府支付，以换取从美国进口的商品。

en: Many millions of Egyptians, needless to say, benefited from this economic assistance, at least in the short term. The supply of power stations, sewage networks, telephone exchanges, and drinking-water plants improved the deteriorated physical fabric, especially in the two metropolises of Cairo and Alexandria, which had been overwhelmed by migration from the countryside following the failure to redistribute a better share of
zh: 不用说，许多埃及人从这种经济援助中受益，至少在短期内如此。发电站、污水管网、电话交换机和饮用水厂的供应改善了破败的物质结构，尤其是在开罗和亚历山大这两个大都市；由于未能向农村人口重新分配更公平的收入份额，它们已被来自乡村的移民淹没，

en: Figure 4. USAID projects by sector, 1975–89. Source: USAID, Status Report (Cairo, 1989).
zh: 图4. 美国国际开发署按部门分列的项目，1975—89年。资料来源：USAID, Status Report (Cairo, 1989).
〔图内文字译释：图内：总额6,282,000,000美元；供水与排污23%、基础设施10%、能源18%、工业8%、人力资源11%、地方政府13%、科学与技术5%、农业12%。〕

en: income among the rural population. At the same time, the aid program exacerbated basic problems in the distribution of wealth and political power, and as several Egyptian scholars argued, came at the price of a crippling dependence on imports of American food, machinery, and technology.

In the 1980s the United States became the largest supplier of Egyptian imports, and by 1988 the country’s imports from America had reached E£1.94 billion. The following year, 1989, they jumped more than 50 percent, to E£2.93 billion.
zh: 与此同时，援助计划加剧了财富和政治权力分配方面的基本问题；并且正如几位埃及学者所论证的，其代价是使该国屈从性地依赖美国粮食、机械和技术的进口。
1980年代，美国成为埃及进口的最大供应国；到1988年，该国从美国的进口达到19.4亿埃镑。次年，1989年，这一数字跃升50%以上，达到29.3亿埃镑。

en: This dependence, and the astronomical levels of debt it caused, gave the United States a powerful position of influence within the Egyptian state. USAID conducted what it termed “cabinet-level dialogue” on macroeconomic policy with the Egyptian government. At times, USAID reported, when this “dialogue” was not “completely successful”—meaning that the Egyptian government rejected or delayed implementing American demands—“annual releases of funds have been delayed.”

Acquiring at every level of the Egyptian bureaucracy this sort of “policy leverage,” as it was called, became the principal criterion according to which USAID development projects in Egypt were evaluated.

And all this was achieved by a program whose larger effect was to provide subsidies to the so-called private sector in the United States—both directly, by the purchase of billions of dollars of its products, and indirectly, by converting Egypt into a future U.S. market.
zh: 这种依赖及其造成的天文数字债务，使美国在埃及国家内部获得了强大的影响力地位。美国国际开发署与埃及政府就宏观经济政策进行它所称的“内阁级对话”。美国国际开发署报告说，有时当这种“对话”并不“完全成功”——意思是埃及政府拒绝或推迟实施美国的要求——“年度资金拨付就被延迟了”。
在埃及官僚机构的每一层级获得这种所谓的“政策杠杆”，成为评估美国国际开发署在埃及发展项目的主要标准。
而这一切都是通过一个其更大效果是向美国所谓私营部门提供补贴的计划实现的——既直接通过购买数十亿美元的美国产品，也间接通过把埃及变成未来的美国市场。

en: opposed to the state?
zh: 反对国家？

en: Thus USAID operated, more or less successfully, as a form of state support to the American corporate sector, while working in Egypt to dismantle state supports. None of this was explained in the discourse of USAID itself, which pretended to stand outside Egyptian politics, conducting merely a “dialogue” at the rational, detached level of “policy.” Yet there is even more that was missing from the discourse of development on Egypt. The $15 billion of assistance between 1974 and 1989 represented only about one-half of U.S. aid to Egypt in that period. The other half consisted of economic assistance to the Egyptian military. From 1985 to 1990 total American aid to Egypt was more than $15 billion, half of which consisted of military aid.

The military aid was largely spent in the United States to purchase weapons, representing in those five years alone a further $7.5 billion of subsidies to U.S. industry. The United States excluded this aid from its figures for “economic assistance,” however, and listed it separately as military aid.
zh: 因此，美国国际开发署作为一种美国企业部门的国家支持形式运作得还算成功，同时在埃及致力于拆解国家支持。所有这一切都没有在美国国际开发署自己的话语中得到解释，该话语假装站在埃及政治之外，仅仅在“政策”的理性、超然层面进行“对话”。然而，关于埃及的发展论述还遗漏了更多东西。1974年至1989年间的150亿美元援助，仅占该时期美国对埃及援助的大约一半。另一半是对埃及军队的经济援助。1985年至1990年，美国对埃及的援助总额超过150亿美元，其中一半是军事援助。
军事援助主要花在美国购买武器，仅这五年就代表了对美国工业另外75亿美元的补贴。然而美国将这项援助排除在“经济援助”数字之外，单独列为军事援助。

en: So American aid, which described its aims in Egypt as the support of the private sector and “pluralism,” in fact channeled half its funds (or more, if one includes the Cash Transfer payments with which America paid back to itself Egypt’s military loans) directly into the most powerful sector of the state. The Egyptian military, with the support of American funds, developed into a major presence within the country’s manufacturing, agriculture, construction, and consumption. Its arms industries, which received state subsidies but whose income went into military rather than national accounts, became the country’s largest manufacturing sector, producing exports (mostly to Iraq) estimated to be worth about three times the total of all other nontextile manufactures.

The army also moved into civilian manufacturing, producing clothes, electrical appliances, construction goods, and pharmaceuticals. In 1986 it negotiated a contract with General Motors to manufacture passenger cars. Under pressure from the American Embassy, USAID pledged General Motors a $200 million subsidy from its aid budget. The project was abandoned for political and financial reasons, but later on the army began to assemble Jeep Cherokees from the Chrysler Corporation.
zh: 因此，美国援助——它在埃及把自己的目标描述为支持私营部门和“多元主义”——实际上把一半资金（如果把美国用现金转移支付来偿还埃及军事贷款给自己也算上，则更多）直接输送到国家最强大的部门。在美国资金支持下，埃及军队发展成为该国制造业、农业、建筑业和消费中的一支主要力量。其军火工业得到国家补贴，但收入进入军事账户而非国家账户，成为该国最大的制造业部门，其出口（主要输往伊拉克）估计约为所有其他非纺织制成品总额的三倍。
军队还进入民用制造业，生产服装、电器、建筑材料和药品。1986年，它与通用汽车谈判达成生产乘用车的合同。在美国大使馆的压力下，美国国际开发署从其援助预算中承诺给通用汽车2亿美元补贴。该项目因政治和财政原因被放弃，但后来军队开始用克莱斯勒公司的吉普切诺基进行组装。

en: Agriculture was another sector in which the military became a dominant presence, setting up dairy, poultry, and vegetable farms, fisheries, land reclamation projects, and food processing industries, particularly in meat, fruit, and vegetables. Its Food Security Division represented the largest agro-industrial enterprise in the country, producing in 1985–86 E£488 million worth of food, or almost one-fifth of the total value of Egyptian food production.

The military also played a leading role in the construction of bridges, roads, power lines, telephone systems, and other civilian infrastructure projects. All these activities provided plentiful opportunities for patronage and personal profit making. The Lockheed Corporation agreed in 1990 to pay a $1 million bribe to an Egyptian member of parliament, who used her influence to persuade the Egyptian military to purchase three of Lockheed’s C-130 Hercules transport planes, giving an indication of some of the sums involved. (When Pentagon auditors discovered the bribe Lockheed promised not to pay it, but then paid it the following year, according to U.S. prosecutors, disguised as a “termination fee.”)

The Ministry of Defense also began to build its own military cities, mostly around Cairo. Thirteen cities were built by 1986, each with a population of 150,000 to 250,000, complete with hospitals, shops, schools, and mosques, and a further ten were under construction.

Together with coastal resorts, tourist services, and elite training colleges, these developments transformed the professional officer class into what Robert Springborg called “an almost entirely autonomous enclave of middleclass modernity in an increasingly impoverished and marginalized Third World economy.”

Meanwhile, many from the most senior ranks, often equipped with diplomas in management from U.S. military colleges, moved on to enjoy the rents from senior positions in ministries, stateowned corporations, and local government.
zh: 农业是军队成为主导力量的另一个部门，它建立了乳业、家禽和蔬菜农场、渔场、垦荒项目和食品加工业，尤其是肉类、水果和蔬菜。其粮食安全司是该国最大的农业综合企业，1985—86年生产了价值4.88亿埃镑的食品，几乎占埃及食品生产总值的五分之一。

军队还在桥梁、道路、输电线路、电话系统和其他民用基础设施项目建设中发挥主导作用。所有这些活动都为庇护和个人牟利提供了大量机会。洛克希德公司1990年同意向一名埃及议员支付100万美元贿赂，后者利用自己的影响力说服埃及军方购买三架洛克希德C-130“大力神”运输机，这显示了所涉部分金额之大。（当五角大楼审计人员发现这笔贿赂时，洛克希德承诺不支付，但据美国检察官称，第二年又支付了，伪装成“终止费”。）
国防部还开始建造自己的军事城市，大多在开罗周边。到1986年已建成十三座城市，每座人口15万至25万，配有医院、商店、学校和清真寺，另有十座正在建设。
连同海滨度假地、旅游服务和精英培训学院，这些发展把职业军官阶层变成了罗伯特·斯普林博格所说的“在一个日益贫困和被边缘化的第三世界经济中几乎完全自治的中产阶级现代性飞地”。
与此同时，许多最高层人士往往持有美国军事学院的管理文凭，转而享受各部委、国有企业和地方政府高级职位的租金。

en: These enclaves of privilege received substantial support from Egyptian public funds. Among the world’s twenty or so lower-middle income countries, Egypt in 1987 came near the bottom of the list in the proportion of central government expenditure devoted to health and education (only Syria and Mexico spent proportionately less) and near the top in the proportion (20 percent) devoted to the military (only Syria, Jordan, North Yemen, and El Salvador spent proportionately more). At the same time, power and privilege on this scale would never have been possible without the multibillion dollar contributions of United States aid.
zh: 这些特权飞地获得了埃及公共资金的大量支持。在世界二十个左右中低收入国家中，1987年埃及在卫生和教育支出占中央政府支出的比例方面接近名单底部（只有叙利亚和墨西哥按比例支出更少），在军事支出比例（20%）方面接近顶部（只有叙利亚、约旦、北也门和萨尔瓦多按比例支出更多）。与此同时，没有美国援助数十亿美元的贡献，这种规模的权力和特权绝不可能存在。

en: Despite its large presence in the Egyptian economy, the large proportion of government funds it consumed, and its even larger proportion of total American support, the military received almost no attention in the literature of organizations like USAID and the World Bank. Given the supposed objectives of developing the private sector and pluralism, the silence of this discourse is astonishing. The silence reflects the necessary limits of the discourse of development. A systematic inquiry into the economy and power of the Egyptian military would have revealed its relations to American military industries, to the system of state subsidies on which those industries depended, and thus to the larger object of American aid programs. In the same way, as I have suggested, a proper analysis of Egyptian agriculture examining the causes of the shift to meat production and the country’s resulting shortages of food and growing indebtedness would have revealed the connections between these events and the crisis of American farming and the remedy of subsidized food exports. Such analyses would serve as a reminder that the discourse of development is situated within, not outside, such relationships.
zh: 尽管军队在埃及经济中大量存在、消耗了很大比例的政府资金、在美国全部支持中占更大比例，但它在诸如美国国际开发署和世界银行的文献中几乎未受关注。鉴于发展私营部门和多元主义的所谓目标，这种话语的沉默令人震惊。这种沉默反映了发展论述的必要限度。对埃及军队的经济和权力进行系统调查，本会揭示它与美国军事工业、与这些工业所依赖的国家补贴体系、从而与美国援助计划更大目标之间的关系。同样，如我所提出的，对埃及农业进行适当分析，考察转向肉类生产的原因以及由此造成的该国粮食短缺和日益沉重的债务，本会揭示这些事件与美国农业危机以及补贴粮食出口这一补救办法之间的联系。这类分析将提醒人们，发展论述位于这类关系之内，而不是之外。

en: That is the reason for the silence. Development discourse wishes to present itself as a detached center of rationality and intelligence. The relationship between West and non-West will be constructed in these terms. The West possesses the expertise, technology, and management skills that the non-West is lacking. This lack is what has caused the problems of the non-West. Questions of power and inequality, whether on the global level of international grain markets, state subsidies, and the arms trade, or the more local level of landholding, food supplies, and income distribution, will nowhere be discussed. To remain silent on such questions, in which its own existence is involved, development discourse needed an object that appeared to stand outside itself. What more natural object could there be, for such a purpose, than the image of a narrow river valley, hemmed in by the desert, crowded with rapidly multiplying millions of inhabitants?
zh: 这就是沉默的原因。发展论述希望把自己呈现为一个超然的理性和智力中心。西方与非西方之间的关系将以这些术语建构。西方拥有非西方所缺乏的专业知识、技术和管理技能。正是这种缺乏造成了非西方的问题。权力和不平等问题——无论是国际粮食市场、国家补贴和军火贸易的全球层面，还是土地占有、粮食供应和收入分配的更地方层面——在任何地方都不会被讨论。为了对这类涉及其自身存在的问题保持沉默，发展论述需要一个看起来站在自身之外的对象。对于这一目的，还有什么对象比一个被沙漠包围、挤满迅速增殖的数百万居民的狭长河谷意象更自然呢？

en: These figures may severely underestimate the proportion of grain fed to animals. The figures for wheat consumption are based on the estimate that animals consumed 18 percent of domestic production, and that this proportion had not increased since 1966 despite the large rise in fodder prices and the relative decrease in the price of imported flour. The actual proportion is difficult to estimate because almost all domestic wheat was consumed within the village. Some sources suggest that 80 percent of domestic wheat was used as fodder (Economist Intelligence Unit, Egypt: Country Report, no. 4, 1989 [London: Economist Intelligence Unit, 1989], 13). If so, then per capita food consumption of grains dropped by 10 percent between 1966 and 1988, and nonfood usage increased by 357 percent to more than 9 million tons—surpassing the 7.45 million tons fed to humans.

en: The success of the East Asian land reforms depended on several factors beside the elimination of large farms, including the development of local village government and agricultural cooperatives, support for rural industry, and the protection of agricultural prices against subsidized U.S. imports. When the Uruguay Round free trade agreements forced the removal of price supports, the Republic of Korea launched the New Agricultural Policy (1994–2004), whose ten-year funding equaled the entire annual budget of the state. The funds supported the development of specialized farms and early retirement for less productive farmers. However, the removal of the three-hectare limit on landholdings immediately encouraged land speculation, which undermined the other aspects of the reform. Hyunseok Oh, “La réforme de la politique agricole en République de Corée, ses défis et ses problèmes: la nouvelle orientation du développement rural face à la libéralisation,” Land Reform 2000/1, 108–17, available at http://www.fao.org/sd/ltdirect/landrf.htm.
zh: 东亚土地改革的成功除消除大农场外，还取决于若干因素，包括发展村庄地方政府和农业合作社、支持农村工业，以及保护农产品价格免受美国补贴进口的冲击。当乌拉圭回合自由贸易协定迫使取消价格支持时，大韩民国启动了新农业政策（1994—2004），其十年资金相当于国家整年的预算。这些资金支持发展专业化农场和让生产力较低的农民提前退休。然而，取消三公顷的土地占有上限立即鼓励了土地投机，削弱了改革的其他方面。Hyunseok Oh, “La réforme de la politique agricole en République de Corée, ses défis et ses problèmes: la nouvelle orientation du développement rural face à la libéralisation,” Land Reform 2000/1, 108–17, available at http://www.fao.org/sd/ltdirect/landrf.htm.

Graham Dyer’s study of data from eighteen Egyptian villages confirms the greater productivity of small farmers, except in the case of one sugarcane-producing village. His evidence, and my own research in the same region, indicates that large cane farmers achieved higher yields by monopolizing the supply of inputs, especially fertilizer. He adds that this would be a good thing, since small farmers can achieve higher yields only by “extreme levels” of self-exploitation—a claim for which there is no evidence. en: As Harriet Friedmann shows, the combination of price supports for farmers, import quotas, and export subsidies was replicated after World War II by the European Community. This postwar international “food regime” generated chronic surpluses and was dependent on forcing open Third World markets by the dumping of food aid and the conversion of these countries to meat consumption. Friedmann, “The Political Economy of Food.”
zh: 正如哈丽雅特·弗里德曼所表明的，二战后欧洲共同体复制了农民价格支持、进口配额和出口补贴的组合。这一战后国际“粮食体制”造成长期过剩，并依赖通过粮食援助倾销和使这些国家转向肉类消费来强行打开第三世界市场。Friedmann, “The Political Economy of Food.”

en: The major hard-currency purchase was the PL 480 Title I food program, amounting to $2.87 billion between 1975 and 1989. PL 480 Title III (canceled after FY 1983) provided an additional $72 million of food, primarily wheat, purchased in Egyptian pounds. The Commodity Import Program (CIP) provided $3.660 billion worth of imports purchased in Egyptian pounds and about $700 million in U.S. dollars. Agricultural commodities and equipment represented one-third of CIP purchases (USAID, Status Report, 1–8, figure 3).

en: By mid-1988 Egypt owed $11.7 billion to the United States, of which $5.7 billion was for military purchases, mostly from the late 1970s and early 1980s. Unlike the easy credit terms given for food and other U.S. imports, these debts were contracted at high fixed interest rates of 12 to 14 percent, and in some cases 18 percent. By the late 1980s interest payments on the military debt to the United States reached $600 million annually. Economist Intelligence Unit, Egypt: Country Report, no. 4, 1989, 56.
zh: 到1988年中，埃及欠美国117亿美元，其中57亿美元用于军事采购，主要来自1970年代末和1980年代初。与食品和其他美国进口品获得的宽松信贷条件不同，这些债务以12%至14%的高固定利率签订，有些甚至达18%。到1980年代后期，对美军事债务的年利息支付达到6亿美元。Economist Intelligence Unit, Egypt: Country Report, no. 4, 1989, 56.

en: U.S. Congress House Committee on Foreign Affairs, Subcommittee on Europe and the Middle East, Hearings on Agency for International Development Policy on the Use of Cash Transfer: The Case of Egypt (Washington, D.C.: 100th Congress, second session, Dec. 10, 1987), 78.The cable leaked to the Washington Post (Feb. 3, 1984) recorded a conversation in Cairo in which the visiting head of USAID asked a high Egyptian official “if the $103 million [cash transfer] would be sufficient to enable the GOE [Government of Egypt] to meet its FMS [Foreign Military Sales] debt servicing obligations through the elections.” USAID officials admitted in Congress that such military use of USAID funds was a violation of the 1978 Security Assistance Act, explained away the cable by saying that Egyptian officials often referred to FMS debt when they meant nonmilitary debt (ignoring the fact that it was the head of USAID, not the Egyptian, who specified FMS debt, and that only an FMS default would trigger adverse political consequences before the elections), and promised that this illegal use of funds would not occur. But despite repeated Congressional requests, USAID produced no accounting of how the Cash Transfers were actually spent. See U.S. Congress, Foreign Assistance Legislation for Fiscal Year 1985, 119–22, 149–52; U.S. Congress, Foreign Assistance Legislation for Fiscal Years 1986–87, 175–78.

en: According to U.S. prosecutors, Lockheed agreed in 1988 to pay a commission of $600,000 per plane to a consulting company owned by the M.P., Layla Takla, and her husband. The Pentagon discovered evidence of the fee agreement in 1989, and Lockheed executives told the Pentagon it would not be paid, but in 1990 the company agreed to pay a $1 million “termination fee” to Takla in lieu of the sale commission. Lockheed pleaded guilty in a case brought under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977 and was fined $24.8 million, twice its profit from the sale. “$24.8 Million Penalty Paid by Lockheed,” New York Times, Jan. 28, 1995, A35.
zh: 据美国检察官称，洛克希德1988年同意向议员莱拉·塔克拉及其丈夫拥有的一家咨询公司支付每架飞机60万美元的佣金。五角大楼1989年发现了这笔费用协议的证据，洛克希德高管告诉五角大楼不会支付；但1990年，该公司同意向塔克拉支付100万美元“终止费”以代替销售佣金。洛克希德在一起根据1977年《反海外腐败法》提起的案件中认罪，被罚款2,480万美元，是其从这笔交易中所得利润的两倍。“$24.8 Million Penalty Paid by Lockheed,” New York Times, Jan. 28, 1995, A35.
